chapter: Big bands, small groups and studio work
title: Studying at Juilliard and now at Capital University

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: It says during the '40s did extensive studies at Julliard which you've already mentioned. Were you basically a full-time student there?
At Julliard?
Yeah.
Oh yeah. I had five subjects. I had Theory, Tympani, Piano, Dictation and what else was it? And Drums.
Did you get a degree?
No, because I couldn't finish there because I was in and out working, going out of town, gigging and things like that and just dropped out, I did.
How close were you to a degree?

Oh goodness, I was quite a distance from a degree, because I didn't continue my studies that much, I didn't have the time. At the time that I was doing Carmen Jones, up there with Raymond Scott, I had that time, you
know I had a little time, but after that, see, I start getting busy and I just couldn't manage to do all that studying and things.
Well you're studying now at Capital University here in Columbus.
Yes.
Did they transfer your credits from Julliard.

Yes, I got some credits from Juilliard and here in Columbus, of course, I'm not doing anything, only on my own, so I can just freelance and do anything I want to do and so that gave me ample time to study.
It's really time consuming to take on one of those subjects.
Oh Lord, I had a conducting class here at Capital, it was 8:00 in the morning, so therefore I had to get up around about 6:30, by the time it took to shower and go there and start conducting.
What kind of ensemble would you conduct?
Large, small.
Like a concert band?
Yes, concert band. Of course they start you off conducting the 'Star Spangled Banner.'
Sure, why not? You have to do it sooner or later.
Oh sure.
Every conductor in the world. Let's see.
